Senator Rafferty, Senate Chair Representative Murphy, House Chair Members of the Joint Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs

Senator Rafferty, Representative Murphy, and Distinguished Members of the Education and Cultural Affairs Committee:
LD 1123, An Act to Provide Funding for MaineCare-related Services for Public Schools, would provide funding to the Maine Department of Education (DOE) to establish two Public Service Coordinator I positions to provide technical assistance support to Maine school administrative units (SAUs) to facilitate MaineCare reimbursements. The Department of Education appreciates the intent of the bill and agrees that this is an appropriate solution to the issue at hand.
As discussed in the Maine Policy Research Institute's presentation on 3/26/2025, many SAUs are currently unable to fully utilize available MaineCare funds to support the funding of special education students, even when those students are utilizing MaineCare-eligible services. School personnel report that MaineCare billing can be technically challenging, with stringent accountability measures which creates hesitancy among Maine SAUs in pursuing these funds. This bill would enable Maine's SAUs to leverage medical funds for medical services that are delivered in schools, thereby preserving education funding for educational services.
By creating these positions, SAUs would be provided with a centralized resource to help them more effectively bill MaineCare for medical expenses that are needed by students within their schools. Explicit points of contact for MaineCare billing support will allow professionals familiar with the needs and programs in schools to address MaineCare related questions to be addressed in concert with experts from the Office of MaineCare Services. Such positions are in line with the Department's own strategic thinking about expanding MaineCare billing in schools.
We are confident in the success of cross-differential collaboration required of these positions. Nonetheless, we recommend clarification of the roles and responsibilities of both the DOE and Department of Health and Human Services to ensure immediate efficacy of the coordination of activities and efforts across the two agencies. We also suggest further consideration of the type of staff (classification) assigned to these positions. Based on the language of the bill, a

Re: LD 1123 - An Act to Provide Funding for MaineCare-related Services for Public Schools
Senator Rafferty, Representative Noonan-Murphy and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs, thank you for the opportunity to provide information neither for nor against LD 1123, An Act to Provide Funding for MaineCare-related Services for Public Schools.
This bill provides ongoing funds to establish two Public Service Coordinator I positions to provide technical assistance and facilitate MaineCare reimbursements for local school districts.
The Department of Health and Human Services (the "Department") supports the addition of staff to facilitate the ongoing collaboration between the Office of MaineCare Services and the Maine Department of Education (DoE) and our joint efforts to improve access to needed services for children as well as to ensure appropriate billing for MaineCare covered services.
If the bill progresses, the Department recommends clarification of the roles and responsibilities of these positions at DoE relative to positions and responsibilities of the Department to ensure coordination of activities and efforts across the two agencies. Relatedly, if these positions required access to the MaineCare billing and claims system (MIHMS) or required technical expertise in MaineCare claims payment or other areas that are the Department's responsibility or specialty, the Department would propose establishing one of these positions within the Office of MaineCare Services where the access and knowledge and related technical supports already reside.
The Department also suggests further consideration of the type of staff (classification) assigned to these positions. Based on the language of the bill, a Public Service Coordinator may be a more senior classification than is appropriate to accomplish the desired tasks.
Please feel free to contact me if you have any questions during your deliberation of this bill.
Sincerely,
Michelle Probert Director Office of MaineCare Services Maine Department of Health and Human Services

Testimony ofSenator Rachel Talbot Ross in support of
LD 1123, "An Act to Provide Funding for MaineCare-related Services for
Public Schools"
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Aflairs April 9, 2025
Senator Rafferty, Representative Murphy, and Honorable Colleagues on the Joint Standing Committee on
Education and Cultural Affairs, I am Senator Rachel Talbot Ross. I represent Senate District 28, which
includes part of my hometown of Portland and Peaks Island. Thank you for the opportunity to speak in support of LD 1123, "An Act to Provide Fundingfor MaineCare-related Services for Public Schools. "
According to the MaineCare in Education 2024 Report, MaineCare member students have two ways to access Medicaid--covered services in Maine schools:
1. Through the provision of IDEA Heath-Related Services. These services are available when a member has an Individualized Education Program (IEP) listing the specific Covered Service(s), as determined by the member's IEP team. Provider requirements and a description of Covered
Service(s) are explained in Part V of the guide, which I have attached to my testimony. MaineCare
does not have oversight of or participate in the IEP process; however, once MaineCare-covered services are listed on a student's IEP. MaineCare can reimburse providers for claims submitted in
accordance with the MaineCare Benefits Manual (MBM).
2. Through the provision of non-IDEA health-related Services. This is when students receive services through a School-Based Health Center or when a provider uses space in a school to deliver services
solely for the convenience of the provider and member.
Through the establishment of two Public Service Coordinator I positions, LD 1123 simply acknowledges
that our ability to adequately and effectively facilitate this access can improve by providing the technical assistance support that Maine school administrative units (SAUs) desperately need.
As this committee knows well, the facilitation of MaineCare reimbursements has been challenging given both how technically difficult MaineCare billing is to process and the strict measures required to qualify
for funding.
The intent of this bill further recognizes what the Maine Policy Research Institute has articulated to this
committee that these complications have, in some instances, had a chilling effect with some SAU's not
going after this critical fimding.

' Testimony of Yusuf Yusuf introducing
LD 1123, An Act to Provide Funding for MaineCare-related Services for
Public Schools Before the Joint Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs
Senator Rafferty, Representative Murphy and members of the Education and Cultural Affairs
Committee, my name is Yusuf Yusuf, and I represent House District 118, which includes part of Portland. I am pleased to present LD 1123, An Act to Provide Funding for MaineCare-related
Services for Public Schools.
Having served on a school board, I have witnessed numerous efforts to establish roles within the district, specifically to manage the complexities of the MaineCare reimbursement process.
School districts often face significant challenges in navigating this system. I believe that initiatives aimed at addressing this issue would not only support the districts themselves but also
provide vital assistance to children and families. With so many students experiencing mental
health challenges, access to Medicaid funding is essential to ensuring they receive the support necessary for academic success.
This bill seeks to fund two full-time MaineCare Coordinator positions within the Department of
Education, both of whom would work directly with local school districts. The two proposed
positions are intended to deliver specialized technical support and serve as key facilitators in streamliningthe MaineCare reimbursement process for local school districts. These roles will be instrumental in ensuring that districts can effectively navigate the administrative and regulatory
complexities associated with Medicaid billing. By enhancing compliance, improving claims
accuracy, and expediting reimbursement timelines, these positions will not only alleviate the operational burden on school persomiel but also maximize the availability of funding for critical
student support services.
Research conducted by the Maine Education Policy Research Institute (MEPRI) at the University of Maine System found that Maine school districts vary widely in their MaineCare billing practices, with many failing to claim all the federal funds they are eligible to receive. In fact,
only 45% of districts participated in reimbursement for eligible services delivered in public
school settings. This represents a missed opportunity, as increased participation could provide a significant source of additional revenue to help offset the growing costs of special education in Maine schools.

District 118: Portland (part)

Unlike larger districts, many smaller districts have historically faced challenges in accessing
these federal funds. These coordinators would support schools throughout the Medicaid application process by clarifying eligible expenses, assisting with necessary documentation, ensuring compliance with federal requirements and helping schools obtain appropriate
A
reimbursement for qualified services. According to the report, MaineCare is a highly complex system, posing a significant barrier for school districts that lack the necessary knowledge, expertise, information systems or time to
manage the billing process. Most Maine school districts reported that they do not bill MaineCare for all eligible services due to the system's complexity, concerns about potential audits and penalties, and the considerable time and effort required to recover even a portion of the costs.
On its own, Maine may lack the resources to fully support school-based mental health services. However, with access to federal Medicaid funding, up to 63% to 70% of these costs could be
covered. Without this assistance, local districts are left to bear the full financial burden--often depending solely on property taxes. This legislation would open the door to tens of millions in federal funds for Maine schools, helping ensure students receive essential mental health support while relieving pressure on local budgets.
Thank you for your time, and I am happy to answer any questions.
